title: The light of the world (John 8:12)
hook: whoever follows me walks not in darkness
tomorrow: The truth shall make you free

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last day of Tabernacles: rivers of living water. Your line was out of his belly. What did you pass on to someone else? Day five hundred seven.

The Easter Vigil begins in the dark. The church is black. Then a single fire is lit outside, and from it one tall candle. A deacon carries it in and stops three times, lifting it, singing the same short phrase: the light of Christ. Each time, people light their small candles from it, and the light moves back through the church, hand to hand, until the whole building glows. What the candle proclaims goes back to one sentence Jesus spoke in the middle of an old feast of lamps. We're still at the feast of Tabernacles.
screen: `THE EASTER VIGIL IN THE DARK.` → `ONE CANDLE, THEN HUNDREDS.` → `BACK TO TABERNACLES.`

segments.voice: Yesterday was water. The feast of Tabernacles also had light. The Jewish sources describe great golden lampstands set up in the temple courts during the feast, so tall that young priests climbed ladders to fill them with oil. The wicks were made from the priests' worn-out garments. The old account says there wasn't a courtyard in Jerusalem that didn't shine with their light, and men danced with torches through the night. Now picture Jesus teaching in the temple, in the treasury, John says, right by that court. And he says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life." It's the second great I am. Bread was what you need every day. Light is what lets you see everything else. And notice the promise. He doesn't say there will be no darkness. He says the one who follows will not walk in darkness. Following is a walking word. A lamp held up ahead on a dark road: you still have to walk, but you can see where to put your feet. We heard the same light at the start of this Gospel: the light shineth in darkness. In Matthew, Jesus turns it around and tells his listeners, you are the light of the world. The Church holds both together: Christ is the light, and those who follow him carry it. That's the Easter Vigil in one gesture. One candle, Christ, risen. Then every hand in the church tipping a small wick toward it, and passing the flame along.
screen: `GOLDEN LAMPS IN THE TEMPLE COURT.` · `THE SECOND GREAT I AM.` · `NOT NO DARK: NOT WALKING IN IT.` · `ONE CANDLE, PASSED ALONG.` · then, large: `THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: walk in the light for a few minutes. If you can, step outside into daylight, or stand by a window, or turn on a lamp and walk slowly across the room toward it. Settle, and breathe. Notice how light changes what you see: edges, colors, faces, your own hands. Walk slowly, feeling each step land. If you pray, you can hold the line, he that followeth me walketh not in darkness. If you don't, just walk and notice the light. The bell holds the time.
The light of the world. The second of John's great I am sayings, spoken in the temple at the feast of lights and water. Today's word.
screen: `THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: not in darkness. Today, when you can't see the whole road, take just the next step you can see. Day five hundred seven.

screen: `DAY 507 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE TRUTH SHALL MAKE YOU FREE.`

howItsDone: At the Easter Vigil Catholics light the paschal candle from a new fire and pass its flame to candles throughout the church, as the deacon sings "the light of Christ" three times.

original.note: Greek: the light of the world (John 8:12).

trapdoor: what you thought: a general saying about Jesus being good.
what it means: spoken at a feast of great lamps, it promises light to walk by for whoever follows.
what a scholar hears: Mishnah Sukkah 5:2–4 describes the golden lampstands and wicks of priestly garments; the treasury (8:20) stood near that court.

sources.quoted: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life.

notes: Tabernacles lamps (golden lampstands, young priests on ladders, wicks from worn priestly garments, every courtyard lit, torch dancing) paraphrased from Mishnah Sukkah 5:2–4. Confirm details.
Whether John 8:12 is set during or just after Tabernacles: John 7:37 is the last day; 7:53–8:11 intervenes. Stated as 'still at the feast'. Confirm.
Easter Vigil: deacon (or priest) sings 'The Light of Christ' three times while processing; people's candles lit after the first or second. Described generally. Confirm.
'The second great I am' follows the count of 6:35 as the first. Confirm.
Audit (10% sample): the hook claimed the Easter Vigil candle rite comes partly from the feast of Tabernacles, which no source supports; it now links only the words of John 8:12 to the rite.
